title: MySQL transactions and isolation
context: What are ACID and the isolation levels in MySQL?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): MySQL questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: ACID means atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability. InnoDB has four isolation levels: READ UNCOMMITTED allows dirty reads, READ COMMITTED avoids them, REPEATABLE READ, the default, gives a stable snapshot for the whole transaction, and SERIALIZABLE locks reads. Plain reads at REPEATABLE READ use one snapshot, while locking reads and writes use gap or next-key locks to stop phantoms. Choose the lowest level that your invariants allow, and keep transactions short.

points.title: Four levels
points.why: Each level trades anomalies against locking and throughput.

points.title: Dirty and phantom reads
points.why: Dirty reads see uncommitted data. Phantoms are new rows appearing in a repeated range query.
